content: When used as an adjective, elective refers to something that is optional and selected, often through a process of choice, such as an election. As a noun, elective refers to an optional subject or course that a student selects as part of their academic curriculum. In the context of education, an elective is an academic course that a student chooses from a range of available options, as opposed to a mandatory or required course. For instance, in an undergraduate psychology program, students may be required to complete six core courses, while also selecting four elective courses from a list of ten available options. In medical education, the term elective can also describe a period of study or clinical training that a medical student undertakes outside their primary medical school, often in a different country or institution.
